claims.text: Deep learning models achieved an approximate 78% relative reduction in classification error on the SST-2 benchmark compared to earlier baseline models.
Squeezed Very Deep Convolutional Neural Networks achieve model size compression of 10x to 20x with an accuracy loss between 0.4% and 1.3%.
FastText incorporates a bag of n-grams as additional features into feed-forward neural networks to capture local word order information.
Early neural word embedding models underperformed classical machine learning models relying on hand-crafted features.
Deep Average Networks outperform syntactic models on text datasets with high syntactic variance.

Section 2.1 notes fastText uses a bag of n-grams as additional features to capture local word order efficiently.

methodologies.name: Comprehensive Literature Survey and Comparative Performance Benchmarking
methodologies.description: A systematic survey categorizing over 150 deep learning text classification architectures and quantitatively analyzing accuracy across 16 benchmark datasets.

limitations.text: Classical machine learning methods depend heavily on hand-crafted features, requiring domain knowledge and feature engineering while failing to generalize or scale with larger training data.
Large neural language models lack grounding, symbolic reasoning capabilities, and interpretability required for mission-critical applications.
The survey explicitly excludes neuro-symbolic hybrid models from its detailed review scope.

future_work.text: Develop new benchmark datasets for complex tasks like multi-step reasoning question answering, multi-lingual text classification, and classification of extremely long documents.
Incorporate commonsense knowledge bases into deep learning models to improve reasoning under incomplete information.
Conduct theoretical and empirical studies to create interpretable deep learning architectures with minimal parameter sizes.
Develop task-agnostic model compression techniques and knowledge distillation frameworks for edge deployment.
Explore zero-shot and few-shot learning techniques leveraging pre-trained language models to minimize target domain labeling requirements.
